I stepped up to run for Congress because I truly believe that a district as diverse as District 30 should be represented not just by someone who understands the struggles facing Angelinos today, but also someone with a deep background of public service. From serving as Legislative Director for Congresswoman Barbara Lee to acting as a senior health advisor to President Biden, I know how Washington works and what needs to change to help make Los Angeles better, more prosperous, and more equal. I feel humbled that out of all the candidates in this crowded primary, Democrats Serve believes that I’m the best candidate for the job. Help me continue my advocacy efforts but on a bigger scale by making a contribution to my campaign for Congress now. body:
We must continue the work to cancel student debt. | |
---
Peter, Student loan payments start back up again next month, and most people can’t afford to pay. **We must urgently cancel all student debt.** President Biden must keep the promise he made to cancel student debt for over 40 million people by pursuing one of the several alternative paths at his disposal to deliver debt relief. [**Together with almost 90 members of Congress, I’ve signed onto a renewed call to action urging President Biden to carry out his commitment to racial justice and Black, brown, and historically excluded communities by using every means available to cancel student debt by early 2024. Will you join me as a grassroots co-signer now?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/P8Elou2Rvc0qoMPEUZrMXcOpy_XqN4R2ZGjoK-5zZnmJ2ealPudhDn-GSDYLriE6ANd7pDJQR2CWyDRYHLwS0O4xNe0a2I_G80BairfaBVtaVP-XBB_4dwUsUONdalCPzoD9sdi9oK-lQdL8RqxFubWSHHUngRhyfamdxThxsUovQiM2C5xIOOgZV4vfOsP0SL9IA-SB-ZHZMSSOG6wTY2rP7jHn7Gx8EwdhYoHXEBxEDVZJNMFe38KdHTGXRkVSxz7wVhn3WmohKMKAngeKzL7Qb2nKu4fD86BYN7ixBPj4oaa-M-_Ac9lMbNa3tHUiL2clfzcMRFjs4CXLTMiD6U6PqX187IlLut46ZsdVtQ4WZPKXMXYjsLBHZlOl_YMH/3zq/GD-5wVKqSXW33FUfaPL2WA/h0/eCQXlsoP5653lYlVMWTv4DwoK-6Q48aFqmgIuh1amJU) **This is a racial and economic justice issue.** Black borrowers have nearly twice as much student debt ($52,700) after four years of college as our white peers ($28,000), and that amount grows with interest. Due to anti-Black racism, Black borrowers’ student debt is often higher than their median annual income. **And not only do Black women carry more student debt than any other group in America, but we carry it the longest.** Last year, President Biden made the historic decision to cancel up to $20,000 in student debt, providing relief to as many as 43 million people. This was undoubtedly the result of years-long organizing by advocates, activists, impacted borrowers, voters who took to the polls in 2020, and progressive lawmakers like myself, who have all called for executive action to address the nearly $2 trillion student loan debt crisis. In June, the U.S. Supreme Court, a cesspool of corruption and misconduct, struck down the president’s plan in a decision that clearly put profits over people and corporations (like Missouri’s student loan company MOHELA) over communities. **This setback is not the end of our campaign to cancel student debt.** The president of the United States has additional tools to provide relief. President Biden must continually find ways to use his authority to cancel student debt, address the rising cost of college, and make higher education affordable for all students who choose that path. [**Join the call for President Biden to use every tool available to cancel student debt by early 2024.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/P8Elou2Rvc0qoMPEUZrMXcOpy_XqN4R2ZGjoK-5zZnmJ2ealPudhDn-GSDYLriE6ANd7pDJQR2CWyDRYHLwS0O4xNe0a2I_G80BairfaBVtmV9HXyu1i1zCnR2jdGVKODNn_vZqye7G3kIk1ks3TTh0vbwvHjI3IdIyMjCmImM0HJcgg0FZNkCWk1QhfR3V-PK3NR6TooFcHW5dtFJ229abydsAdI9Oxni_Lcuzc4E6Oebt7Wpquii2Maa70zsoX67Iaw-jWVSibwlvmjae3Y1lKLV2J5EIArdkAlgHRpC4cnkRRGCGInC58_kqvYgHX7WuKiv02PGw47m3baTPP9IGMWaSKZ7a43vWg--iPTVCUGSuwfX43sBhGDn25l1m7/3zq/GD-5wVKqSXW33FUfaPL2WA/h1/HFx60y9oJTmH5rSkDBw0kM2Ol8S_l_KQeX5isPAci5I) **[SIGN ON](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/P8Elou2Rvc0qoMPEUZrMXcOpy_XqN4R2ZGjoK-5zZnmJ2ealPudhDn-GSDYLriE6ANd7pDJQR2CWyDRYHLwS0O4xNe0a2I_G80BairfaBVtbLSdADj3mxAn_p60ED2VXRswGj_P25vP8g4rMetGI3Ui_mX5eqB4GInlosX42PUkiTL3KdlqYeJv9wELbUX1p_s7RMK70OFEBekHQCXn9x2Ox2NAIfxxhuVuYroKc93niJqGDitH5tt_mfngm1qCV_Pfx6FjYDLKSBLErNVz5p7rmWhIA5gyDj-F0JxrhC6HW0ReEUuDNQ0BE6krxU_JbqCQTIOBMfpjijbdpckQHjZaZt3D-pcWO9jQos4mfiU0n1aqG23FUuLS5RuNEWix4/3zq/GD-5wVKqSXW33FUfaPL2WA/h2/Msec_7AYjdQvT-wGa5Th8qNR-MqBs9gMIlUHLSu7wPE) ** Especially in the wealthiest country in the world, no one should go into debt to receive a higher education. **I want to see all student debt canceled. I know how hard it is to walk through life with that burden.** For many people, the burden of student debt is never-ending. Nearly three million people over the age of 62 owe more than $110 billion in federal student loans and almost one-third of them are in default, putting these seniors at risk of having their Social Security benefits garnished. Almost **half of Latino borrowers would have their entire debt forgiven by canceling $20,000** , and canceling at least **$50,000 in debt would increase the wealth of Black Americans by 40% nationwide.** Now, imagine the impact of canceling _all_ student debt. This is why our work must not stop. All of our economic policy decisions must be universal and rooted in racial, gender, and economic justice at their core. In order to reduce the racial wealth gap and advance a just and equitable economy for all, we must alleviate the burden of student debt and ensure universal access to higher education. **Nothing is off the table, except inaction.** [**Join us in the call to President Biden to cancel student debt. Add your name as a grassroots co-signer now.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/P8Elou2Rvc0qoMPEUZrMXcOpy_XqN4R2ZGjoK-5zZnmJ2ealPudhDn-GSDYLriE6ANd7pDJQR2CWyDRYHLwS0O4xNe0a2I_G80BairfaBVsjfpCEQWz1oCULG6CPrnOGCX_aiL-mDsLmFzxYpo9_bBhFLVfHfVxSbu20FhrO3AqS0nxeILpfbnNOunELrUxmcwqlU2yM6iZ5H_5kh4Xcmyi0QMTlmEtrIiN0cSPVmn0SKJO4_AEZQ2gK_eo-nXpo1nJ9Cu_h7amtnzmCZ7JXODZYVPiU5qIinMzb2YsS6QOQcrdaAse8ccOW-xFzD00-1qjLaYzDw03woM5sptWuIE_LeDPt3jBtedUroAtTCOk9R1wZiRyST7E6SuQL1upm/3zq/GD-5wVKqSXW33FUfaPL2WA/h3/qzT35cJ44Z2gOgqqfeYddjqpEow3w6JG9jZ8TteSCBE) With love, Cori **[SUPPORT OUR MOVEMENT](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/wehEm_vu1NBVXOKYSqOxTOi34aJoCJC1EivM7Ih953yR4PRT3K3B8IqGQv2cv0ERbbYt-Yl5U13JBU2kSsmGMwfzFCrGkwmqRx-M4DSl4dKsyIBQ23WEnR_ObprkFhJzYLrJj-7BTLwxk1smhqUGL3xk_biiqXLkfDv3r4Gg1tD9mGDuSn2uA0ygTePq1kJ6K4B7ZZ0sN2srYcUPrvxZM2JC3A3rVBQopJfljxHovlCdrdzzL439t9iscnok48Tk6eRFLYGyl11BXB5QinweB6pMup2t4dmfz2COElJ8R_kqgBjy72zD51Q95YkHgb_4tBICSQy0g_mUtn-1RxISj-oWbpVYszRoWgs7s7jMaOv-wVdR6BsbDVBeyULaBS-tdJyZR3WCRNP1MNYMbYTkbdGbciun7N_XZhrco8RF46232R7qTFUBHO7ElC5Lw5Mg/3zq/GD-5wVKqSXW33FUfaPL2WA/h4/NTLPPEBdh2BtlNMVKgqmSg5NsUE1gy2LMvmXbUhSFTU) **

This was undoubtedly the result of years-long organizing by advocates, activists, impacted borrowers, voters who took to the polls in 2020, and progressive lawmakers like myself, who have all called for executive action to address the nearly $2 trillion student loan debt crisis. In June, the U.S. Supreme Court, a cesspool of corruption and misconduct, struck down the president’s plan in a decision that clearly put profits over people and corporations (like Missouri’s student loan company MOHELA) over communities. This setback is not the end of our campaign to cancel student debt. The president of the United States has additional tools to provide relief. President Biden must continually find ways to use his authority to cancel student debt, address the rising cost of college, and make higher education affordable for all students who choose that path. Especially in the wealthiest country in the world, no one should go into debt to receive a higher education. I want to see all student debt canceled. I know how hard it is to walk through life with that burden. For many people, the burden of student debt is never-ending. Nearly three million people over the age of 62 owe more than $110 billion in federal student loans and almost one-third of them are in default, putting these seniors at risk of having their Social Security benefits garnished. Almost half of Latino borrowers would have their entire debt forgiven by canceling $20,000 , and canceling at least $50,000 in debt would increase the wealth of Black Americans by 40% nationwide. Now, imagine the impact of canceling all student debt. This is why our work must not stop. All of our economic policy decisions must be universal and rooted in racial, gender, and economic justice at their core. In order to reduce the racial wealth gap and advance a just and equitable economy for all, we must alleviate the burden of student debt and ensure universal access to higher education. Nothing is off the table, except inaction. With love, Cori Paid for by Cori Bush for Congress | | Sent via . subject: MADE IN MICHIGAN PANEL!!!
body:
Announcing Congressmen John Moolenaar, Tim Walberg, Jack Bergman for a Made in Michigan Panel hosted by Justin Barclay. | | |
---
| |
---
| |
# Party of the Constitution
---
A “Made in Michigan Congressional Panel” featuring Michigan Congressmen Rep. John Moolenaar, Rep. Tim Walberg, and Rep. Jack Bergman and will be hosted by Radio Host Justin Barclay has been confirmed for the Mackinac Leadership Conference.
The **NEW MIGOP** , led by the **CONSTITUTIONALISTS ,** is committed to making this conference the best one yet. The “Made in Michigan Panel” joins an already impressive lineup of speakers, which includes JIM CAVIEZEL, KARI LAKE, VIVEK RAMASWAMY, ZUBY, ALEX NEWMAN, and TAMARA SCOTT.
We are confident that the upcoming Mackinac Republican Leadership Conference will be the most diverse and unforgettable one ever.
Justin’s Barclay parents will tell you he was born with a microphone in his hand. So, it’s no wonder his radio career started even before he was out of high school. He’s been heard in major markets all across the country, including Philadelphia, Detroit, Tampa, Cincinnati, & Louisville, but fondly calls West Michigan (Grand Rapids) home. Justin is a frequent guest host for the nationally syndicated Glenn Beck program, heard on over 300 radio stations coast to coast.
Today, he engages guests and listeners in lively conversations about national and local topics while talking about what matters most in West Michigan. Justin has won multiple ‘Awards for Broadcast Excellence’ from The Michigan Association of Broadcasters and is honored to continue serving the community on and off of the legendary airwaves of WOOD Radio. Tune in on weekdays at 9 am to 106.9FM or 1300AM for Justin’s one-hour podcast called West Michigan Live with Justin Barclay. And if you live in the Detroit area, be sure to check out Justin’s new show, Justin Mornings Detroit's News Talk, weekdays from 6-9 a.m. on 910AM Superstation.
The daytime coverage for the 910AM Superstation includes the metro Detroit area and extends to the northern lower peninsula of Michigan, south to northern Ohio and Indiana, west into the Grand Rapids area, and east into Ontario, Canada.
Congressman John Moolenaar represents the hardworking residents of Michigan’s Second Congressional District. As Michigan’s senior member of the House Committee on Appropriations, Moolenaar is dedicated to holding the federal government accountable to taxpayers. He strongly believes in fiscal responsibility and has been fighting to make the economy work for Michigan families and seniors. As a member of the committee, he serves on the Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies and the Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies.
Moolenaar brings years of leadership experience in the private and public sectors to Congress. He began his career as a chemist after graduating from Hope College with a bachelor’s degree in chemistry. Moolenaar then worked in business development and as a school administrator. Moolenaar has a master’s degree in public administration from Harvard University. From 2003-2008, he served in the Michigan House of Representatives and in the Michigan State Senate from 2011-2015. Congressman Moolenaar and his wife, Amy, raised their family in Michigan and are blessed with six children and two grandchildren.
Tim Walberg is currently serving his eighth term in Congress as the representative of southern Michigan. The diverse constituency of Michigan’s 5th District encompasses Branch, Cass, Hillsdale, Jackson, Lenawee, Monroe, and St. Joseph Counties, along with portions of Berrien, Calhoun, and Kalamazoo Counties. Prior to his time in public office, Tim served as a pastor in Michigan and Indiana, as president of the Warren Reuther Center for Education and Community Impact, and as a division manager for Moody Bible Institute. He also served in the Michigan House of Representatives from 1983 to 1999 and is proud to bring his reputation as a principled legislator, fiscal reformer, and defender of traditional values to Washington.
Based on his record of legislative accomplishment, Tim was ranked by the Center for Effective Lawmaking, a nonpartisan collaboration between Vanderbilt University and the University of Virginia, as the most effective member of Michigan's congressional delegation in the 115th Congress. In the following session of Congress, the Center for Effective Lawmaking once again recognized Tim for his policy-making success, naming him the top Republican legislator on technology issues. In the 118th Congress, Tim serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and the House Education and the Workforce Committee. He and his wife, Sue, have been married for 48 years, love being grandparents, and enjoy spending time outdoors and riding on their Harley. They live in Tipton, Michigan, where they raised their three children: Matthew, Heidi, and Caleb.
Growing up in the Midwest, Jack Bergman’s parents instilled in him the values that drive the American Dream: If you work hard, never quit, and strive for excellence, you will find success. Those values are what guided him to the rank of Lt. General in the United States Marine Corps, empowered him to successfully own and operate a small business, and allowed him to enjoy a 22-year career as a commercial airline pilot.
Jack proudly represents the First District of Michigan. The boundaries contain the entire Upper Peninsula and all of the northern Lower Peninsula. Altogether, the district makes up about 44% of the land mass of the state of Michigan. The Bergman family's roots in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula stretch back to the late 1800s when his ancestors worked as iron miners. Serving his country in uniform for 40 years, Jack has spent time all around the United States – and the world. Nearly three decades ago, Jack and his wife Cindy settled in Watersmeet, on the western edge of Michigan’s beautiful Upper Peninsula.
Jack is a grandfather to ten grandchildren. This has always been one of the largest factors in his service in Congress. When Jack sees what is happening in Washington, he knows that we are not doing our best at leaving our children and grandchildren a better place. From his business to his distinguished military career and now in Congress - Jack Bergman does not accept the status quo as an acceptable path forward. Jack is driven by his commitment to serving others. While in the military, he launched two successful startup businesses in the medical equipment field, maintaining an obligation to both his nation and his customers simultaneously. As an entrepreneurial leader focused on mission accomplishment and customer satisfaction, Jack knows how to get things done.
Hard work and commitment made the United States the most exceptional nation in the world. Those are the principles that have guided Jack’s life and are the principles that he is bringing to Washington. He believes what most Michiganders believe: Americans know how to live their lives better than politicians or bureaucrats do. Jack’s life has been dedicated to service and defending the Constitution. He is the highest-ranking combat Veteran to have ever served in the U.S. House. He is shaking up the status quo in both Congress and will continue defending the United States from those who want to weaken it, both domestically and abroad.

name: Katie Porter
subject: Throwback to 2012, at Elizabeth Warren’s Election Night
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Katie Porter for Senate
body:
Elizabeth Warren and I met long before either of us imagined ourselves running for office.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/14558?t=1&akid=30131%2E3422442%2EwhpmYS)
Derek, Elizabeth Warren and I met long before either of us imagined ourselves running for office. You see, Elizabeth was my law professor and later a mentor as we practiced consumer protection law.
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-20230919-1?refcode=EMAL19_1_EW_20230919_V1_F&refcode2=30131_3422442_whpmYS&akid=30131%2E3422442%2EwhpmYS)_Here we are at her Election Night party in 2012!_
Elizabeth was elected to the Senate in 2012, but it wasn’t until 2016, when Donald Trump was elected, that I considered running myself. When I told Elizabeth about my idea to run for Congress in my Republican-held district, she offered valuable advice and support—she was the first person to endorse my campaign.
**Early on she told me,_nobody_ gets elected alone.**
That message has stayed with me through three competitive House races and throughout this Senate campaign. From the volunteers who have answered phones, knocked doors, and set up offices, to the grassroots donors who have pitched in $5 whenever they can, I am so grateful for every person who has gotten our campaign to this point.
[**In that spirit, I’m asking if you can join our team today by making your first contribution to our Senate campaign.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-20230919-1?refcode=EMAL19_1_EW_20230919_V1_F&refcode2=30131_3422442_whpmYS&akid=30131%2E3422442%2EwhpmYS)
[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-20230919-1?refcode=EMAL19_1_EW_20230919_V1_F&refcode2=30131_3422442_whpmYS&akid=30131%2E3422442%2EwhpmYS)
There are still five months to go before our competitive primary, and this is going to be a team effort. From telling your friends and neighbors about our campaign and reminding them to vote, to pitching in $3, this campaign will be successful only because of grassroots support.
I can’t do this alone, and I’m so appreciative of your support!
Katie

Katie is running for the U.S. Senate because Californians deserve a warrior fighting for them in Washington. Our campaign is people-powered, we don’t take a dime from corporate PACs, federal lobbyists, or executives from Big Oil or Big Pharma. **[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-footer?refcode=EMAL19_1_EW_20230919_V1_F&t=2&refcode2=30131_3422442_whpmYS&akid=30131%2E3422442%2EwhpmYS)**

I'm writing to thank you for all of your support and ask you to support my most important event of the year. **I'm hosting my annual virtual Build Our America event on Tuesday, September 26th at 5pm PT / 8pm ET!**
**We have a very special guest speaker this year: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez!** This will be a unique opportunity to hear directly from me and AOC about the future of our movement and our work fighting for progressive values in Congress.

name: Lose Cruz PAC
subject: An (incomplete) list of Ted's worst moments
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LOSE CRUZ PAC
body:
If you need a midday laugh, we’re here to help.
# [](https://act.losecruzpac.com/go/128?t=1&akid=96%2E623276%2EltpvTn)
Part-time Senator Ted Cruz can’t ever seem to get out of his own way.
After being elected in 2012 as a self-described “darling” of the Tea Party movement, Cruz quickly made a name for himself by...becoming an embarrassment to Texas.
**[If you don't have the time to laugh with us but still want to make a difference in our mission of losing Cruz, please chip in $5 today!](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-lc-20230919?refcode=em20230919&amount=5&refcode2=96_623276_ltpvTn&akid=96%2E623276%2EltpvTn)**
While there are _way_ too many examples to list, here are some of the worst: ⬇️
1. During her confirmation hearings last year, Ted asked now Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson if she thought babies were racist (we wish we were joking) 🙄

[](https://act.losecruzpac.com/go/1408?t=2&akid=96%2E623276%2EltpvTn)

2. While running for reelection in 2018, Ted claimed that Beto O'Rourke — his opponent at the time — wanted to ban BBQ in Texas❓ (Unclear if this was his attempt at making a joke)

3. In a failed attempt to gut the Affordable Care Act, Ted _**not only**_ engineered a needless government shutdown but also extended his unnecessary filibuster by forcing his Senate colleagues to listen to him read Dr. Seuss.

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-lc-20230919?refcode=em20230919&amount=5&refcode2=96_623276_ltpvTn&akid=96%2E623276%2EltpvTn)

4. In a truly bizarre moment during the 2016 presidential campaign, Ted’s wife, Heidi, shared that the first thing they did after their honeymoon was purchase “literally 100 cans of Campbell’s Chunky soup.” Completely normal!

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-lc-20230919?refcode=em20230919&amount=5&refcode2=96_623276_ltpvTn&akid=96%2E623276%2EltpvTn)

5. And last but certainly not least — in February 2021, as Texans were freezing in their homes during an unprecedented winter storm, what did their junior senator do in response? Ted decided to flee to Cancun and once he was rightfully condemned, he threw his wife and kids under the bus 🚍.

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-lc-20230919?refcode=em20230919&amount=5&refcode2=96_623276_ltpvTn&akid=96%2E623276%2EltpvTn)
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-lc-20230919?refcode=em20230919&amount=5&refcode2=96_623276_ltpvTn&akid=96%2E623276%2EltpvTn)(What a stand-up guy)

All jokes aside, we’re tired. Tired of these antics. Tired of being embarrassed perpetually by a man who would rather spend his days doing anything other than working on behalf of Texans.
**That's why the Lose Cruz team is hard at work to build the massive grassroots coalition it's going to take to finally send our jet-setting senator into early retirement for good. But we can't do this without you.**
**[So if you can, will you chip in any amount today to Lose Cruz?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-lc-20230919?refcode=em20230919&amount=&refcode2=96_623276_ltpvTn&akid=96%2E623276%2EltpvTn)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-lc-20230919?amount=5&refcode=em20230919&refcode2=96_623276_ltpvTn&akid=96%2E623276%2EltpvTn)**
More to come,
— Lose Cruz PAC

And as we speak, Republican state officials are laying out their extremist agendas to seize power by rigging the new round of legislative redistricting to deny Americans fair and equal representation. When barriers to voting single out specific groups of Americans—Black Americans, Native Americans, young voters, and college students—it's pure partisan manipulation, and it corrupts elections. It's absolutely wrong. Voting is the heart of our democracy, and everyone deserves the same chance to cast a ballot and know their vote counts. clean_body: | | | | Our democracy depends on people like you and me exercising our constitutional right to vote. For generations, people in our country were denied that right, and our democracy suffered for it. But countless activists – some famous, others unknown – fought for laws that recognized that every American, regardless of gender, skin color, bank balance, or religion, has the right to participate in choosing our leaders. Voting gives the people the power. Today is National Voter Registration Day, so I'm asking you to make sure you're registered to vote. Now, is your family registered to vote? Your friends? It's on all of us to build a better future for the next generation. But we can only do it if we make our voices heard. Participation is everything when it comes to elections, and voting is the most effective way we can make our voices heard. So many elections are decided by just a handful of votes. Never doubt that your vote matters and your voice makes a difference. Voting is one of the most important things we do as citizens. Today is the perfect day to make sure you are registered. | | **For Immediate Release:** September 19, 2023
**Contact:**[press@davemin.com](mailto:press@davemin.com)
**Local Dem Clubs Support Dave Min**
_Min Consolidates Party Support Ahead of Endorsement Convention
With Resounding Leads In Local Straw Polls_ **IRVINE, CA** — California State Senator Dave Min remains undefeated, and continues to secure victories in each straw poll nominating contest across Orange County. In the third of its kind, the Irvine Democratic Club voted with a resounding 93% to recommend Dave Min for the Democratic Party’s endorsement. Other victories include the Central OC Dems and the instrumental Democrats of Greater Irvine, a group of activists who were key to flipping Orange County Blue in 2018 and have continued to help build out Democratic infrastructure in the region. **“Fundraising, endorsements and now straw polling is all saying the same thing,”** said Dan Driscoll, Campaign Manager at Dave Min for Congress.**“Dave is building a wide, grassroots coalition of support. Teachers, law enforcement, labor and party activists agree: Dave Min is the candidate to keep CA-47 Blue. Republicans know it–that’s why Scott Baugh needs national Republicans’ help to keep pace with this campaign. And Democrats know it too–that’s why Dave has yet to lose a straw poll.”** Handily winning straw polls in Irvine is welcome support for any candidate seeking to win a Democratic nominating contest in the area.**The Democratic stronghold of Orange County, Irvine is home to the vast majority of registered Democrats in California's 47th District, with 39.58%**. Inside Elections put it best last week: “Min has a base of support in Irvine, where much of the district’s Democratic votes come from, and inroads with the district’s substantial Asian American population.” **The AAPI voter share in the district sits around 19%**. And while straw polls can provide some indication of the level of enthusiasm for a given candidate, they may not be the most scientific form of surveying the political landscape. That’s why the Min campaign turned this summer to Public Policy Polling, a well-respected, national firm that found Sen. Min with a strong lead over likely-Republican opponent, Scott Baugh. Those polling numbers are available [here](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=a3559ec122&e=7017cc100e). Min has consolidated support from local, state, and national endorsers. Min entered the race with support from current CA-47 Representative, Katie Porter. In recent months, Min has announced the endorsements of California Lieutenant Governor Eleni Kounalakis, Attorney General Rob Bonta, State Treasurer Fiona Ma, Insurance Commissioner Ricardo Lara, Superintendent of Public Schools Tony Thurmond, the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus’s political leadership ASPIRE PAC, more than 50 local Orange County government officials, and more than 60 state legislators. He is labor’s candidate in this race as well, recently receiving the recommendation of the Orange County Labor Federation, as well as SEIU, IBEW, CFT, OCEA, LAPPL, UFCW, CWA, IUPAT and Teamsters. A full endorsement list is available [here](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=c4e43404ba&e=7017cc100e). Senator Min, the only Korean-American in the state legislature, serves as Chair of the Senate Natural Resources and Water Committee and as Senate Vice Chair of the Asian and Pacific Islander Legislative Caucus. Min has proven himself an incredibly effective legislative leader in the Senate, authoring 16 bills signed into law by the Governor, including leading legislation on hate crimes, gun violence prevention, family safety, and women’s reproductive rights. In the wake of the 2021 Huntington Beach Oil Spill, he stood up to the oil industry and led efforts to end offshore drilling. Min serves as Chair of the Senate Natural Resources and Water Committee and as Senate Vice Chair of the Asian and Pacific Islander Legislative Caucus. He previously chaired the Senate Cybersecurity Select Committee.** ** Before entering the State Senate, Min was a law professor at UC Irvine, where he taught and researched in the area of business law. He resides with his wife Jane Stoever, a UC Irvine law professor who specializes in domestic violence and family law, and their three children in Irvine. Dave is a native Californian, a product of California public schools who graduated from the Wharton School and Harvard Law School, and an Eagle Scout.
#####
_California’s 47th is an open Congressional District in Orange County that includes the Cities of Costa Mesa, Huntington Beach, Irvine, Newport Beach, and Seal Beach, and portions of Laguna Beach, Laguna Hills, and Laguna Woods. Incumbent Katie Porter is vacating the seat to run for U.S. Senate. In 2022, Porter defeated former Assemblymember Republican Scott Baugh by 3.44% in this “toss-up” district. State Senator Dave Min currently represents over 80% of Congressional District 47 in Sacramento. In 2020, Min received over 158,000 votes within CA-47, defeating incumbent John Moorlach by 5.15%. 19% of the registered voters in CA-47 are of Asian and Pacific Islander descent, including one of the largest Korean-American populations in the country._

| From addressing the crucial ongoing issue of mental health and substance abuse, to fighting for the future of farming in our district... it's been a busy month!

Check out some key highlights below, follow me on social media to stay up-to-date, and as always, I am grateful for your support.
---
|
---
|
---
Mental health and substance abuse disorders are at a crisis point and we need to make them a priority.

This past month, I brought public officials, health and mental health professionals and law enforcement together to have productive conversations surrounding those crucial issues.

Later on in the month, I had a great conversation with Paul Ciliberto on Cilberto & Friends on his podcast on the same topics.

\- "[Addressing mental health and substance use disorders topic of Sullivan roundtable (VIDEO)](https://molinarofordutchess.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b7a5de207e774ea8a3851d76c&id=553d74a326&e=a39a20e5dd)"
\- "[Ciliberto & Friends Podcast](https://molinarofordutchess.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b7a5de207e774ea8a3851d76c&id=58aee4abb1&e=a39a20e5dd)"
|
---
|
---
The pending Farm Bill is vitally important legislation that affects the future of farming and agriculture, both nationally and here at home.

I recently toured Stone Ridge Orchards and talked with the owner, Elizabeth Ryan, to stand in support of our farmers and I'll continue to fight to ensure they get the resources they need.

[\- "Area House members tour Ulster farm ahead of new farm bill"](https://molinarofordutchess.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b7a5de207e774ea8a3851d76c&id=ad413ee071&e=a39a20e5dd)
[\- "Farm bill deadline approaches as lawmakers list priorities"](https://molinarofordutchess.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b7a5de207e774ea8a3851d76c&id=8dea94d4ae&e=a39a20e5dd)
|
---
|
---
We had a great turnout at the Senior Resource Fair at the American Legion Post 1645 in Binghamton. It was an opportunity to highlight the support, services, and resources that they need and are available to them.

[\- "Molinaro hosts a senior resource fair](https://molinarofordutchess.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b7a5de207e774ea8a3851d76c&id=d3ec8a6811&e=a39a20e5dd)["](https://molinarofordutchess.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b7a5de207e774ea8a3851d76c&id=f6d24bffb6&e=a39a20e5dd)
|
---
|
---
I sent a letter on behalf of the Glen Aubrey residents who, without warning, had their Post Office shut down on them. I'll keep working on their behalf to ensure they get the services they are owed.

Folks,
Growing up, I had one Barbie doll, Air Force Barbie to be specific, which was a gift from a relative and reference to my grandmother who served in the branch in real life. She came with shorter hair, a flight suit, and pearl earrings. My active-duty Navy mom was not a Barbie fan, but I was allowed to keep the gift and dressed her up in orphaned socks that I had transformed into ball gowns.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/teamlesley_email?refcode2=img_photos [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/teamlesley_email?refcode2=img_photos]Yup! That’s little me, Grandma in uniform, and the kind of Barbie I had!
Here's the thing, while baby dolls were traditionally marketed to little girls so they could pretend to be parents, Barbie is a grown-up who takes care of herself. With a little imagination and determination, Barbie can be anything.
I love being a mom and raising my sons. But like Barbie, I’ve never limited myself to just one dream.
Student loans, financial aid, and lots of jobs cooking and cleaning houses helped me earn my college degree. I worked as a journalist and later as a staffer on the Hill before running for and winning a seat in the Maryland House of Delegates. But I'm not done yet.
Maryland’s 6th District has been represented by over forty men and only two women. It’s been 30 years since the last woman was elected to the House from our district! Our state has not had a woman in federal office since Senator Barbara Mikulski. And nationally, only 6.8% of Congress members are moms with kids under 18. It’s time to change that. It's time to show today's children that just like Barbie, women can achieve whatever we set our minds to.
I’m ready to take on a broken Congress to finally pass reasonable gun safety measures on the federal level, address the opioid crisis, and always protect Social Security, Medicare, and our reproductive freedoms.
I’m asking, will you be one of 27 people we need to give today to stay on track to meeting our end-of-quarter fundraising goal? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/teamlesley_email?refcode2=link_CTA] Anything you give — whether it’s $25, $50, $100, or the most generous amount you can — will help in a meaningful way.
Our society and Barbie’s development into a feminist icon have come a long way since she was introduced in 1959. Still, we've got a lot of work left to do.
In the legislature, I’ve led the fight to protect our reproductive rights, earned bipartisan support banning illegal ghost guns, closed the gap of healthcare workers in rural areas, and lowered childcare costs for Maryland families like mine.
Now, I’m running for the only Congressional district that’s in play this cycle in Maryland. Unlike virtually every other race here, there will be a highly competitive primary and general election. Let me tell you, it’s going to take a tough woman to keep this swing seat blue.
I hope you'll chip in $25, $50, $100, or what you can today to keep this competitive open seat blue and send a proven woman leader to Congress. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/teamlesley_email?refcode2=link_CTA2]
We've got a big goal left to meet this quarter, and your support will make a huge difference.
- Lesley
When she’s not busy being a mom to her two toddlers, Lesley Lopez serves the people of Maryland as a Delegate from District 39 in the Maryland General Assembly. Since she was first elected in 2018, Lesley has rapidly become an effective legislator and leader, spearheading efforts to alleviate student debt, improve the delivery and efficiency of health care, and protect the limited financial resources of economically vulnerable Marylanders. Lesley has passed legislation to strengthen gun safety laws and guarantee the rights for all women in the state. She is an adjunct professor at George Washington University and a proud union member of SEIU Local 500. Lesley lives in Germantown, MD, with her husband Richard Kelly, and their two sons, Max and Graham.

Friend, these numbers are shocking.
The Census Bureau just released its annual report, which includes numbers on childhood poverty in the United States.
It showed that five million children were plunged into poverty last year. You read that correctly: five million kids.
https://secure.michaelbennet.com/a/x_071023_ctceitc [https://secure.michaelbennet.com/a/x_071023_ctceitc]
Based on data from the Census Bureau [https://www.census.gov/library/publications/2023/demo/p60-280.html]
What changed? Well, in 2021, Michael led Congress in the passage of a major expansion of the Child Tax Credit. Millions of families benefited, including 90% of Colorado's kids.
But Congress let the expanded Child Tax Credit expire after one year. And our nation's kids are much worse off because of it.
Michael has been fighting for the expanded Child Tax Credit since 2015. When it was enacted in 2021, it cut child poverty nearly in half. It was a huge win for working families who desperately needed relief during the pandemic.
Now, we’re seeing the backslide. This report makes it clear — by failing to renew the expansion, Congress left millions of kids behind.
Michael is fighting hard to pass the Working Families Tax Relief Act to once again expand the Child Tax Credit, and this time, make it permanent. Becoming a citizen co-sponsor shows the tremendous grassroots support Michael has behind this bill. Will you sign on now? [https://secure.michaelbennet.com/a/x_071023_ctceitc]

We need to renew Michael's Child Tax Credit so every kid has the opportunity to get ahead.

name: Gavin Newsom
subject: This is how crazy things have gotten
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CAMPAIGN FOR DEMOCRACY PAC
body:
Just last week two out of three 9th Circuit Court judges threw out California's first-in-the-nation ban on marketing guns to kids.

Friends -
I don't know if you all saw this, but just last week two out of three 9th Circuit Court judges tossed out California's first-in-the-nation ban on marketing guns to kids.
Guns like the JR-15. I kid you not. Look at this:
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cfd-c-em-sept23?refcode=em230919&refcode2=1574_4767699_0uO__v&akid=1574%2E4767699%2E0uO__v)
Google it if you don't believe me.
The marketing for this thing was the skulls of young babies with a green pacifier and a pink pacifier – one for a little boy and one for a little girl.
That is how perverted and crazy things have gotten.
And judges said we didn't have the right to ban ads like that, like when Joe Camel was trying to sell cigarettes to kids.
They said we couldn't do that.
So we can feel powerless and we can give into cynicism, or we can actually do something. Because we have agency here.
I want to go on the offense. And with our fight to pass a Constitutional Amendment to make our communities safer from gun violence, that is what we are doing.
Thank you,
Gavin Newsom
* * *
👋🏻 Wait ... Before you click away! 🇺🇸
Now that California became the first state to call for a Constitutional Amendment on gun safety, we need to get this thing introduced and passed in other states.
That takes work. It takes organizing. And it's work we are committed to doing. But Gavin Newsom can't do it alone.
So please. If contributing $20 today feels like it's worth expanding this effort to other states, make that donation here. It's people like you who will help us continue to make progress on this issue. Thank you.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: My interview with Vox on how we can finally regulate Big Tech
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
The tech industry has shut down every attempt to regulate it or impose liability on it. Enough is enough.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=69%2E4032634%2EsWk6kr)
---
Here's the way I see it: We cannot let a handful of unelected Big Tech billionaires govern our lives and govern our democracy. The digital revolution has given us amazing new innovations, but it’s come with a real dark side. Big Tech companies have exploited people’s data, invaded Americans’ privacy, and crushed competition without accepting any liability — and Congress is not responding. **So I recently introduced a bipartisan bill to create a Digital Consumer Protection Commission, an agency with the flexibility and the expertise to take on Big Tech giants like Meta, Google, and Amazon.** [**I was recently interviewed by Vox to talk about this new agency and how it would protect consumers from their abusive business practices (kind of like the CFPB!). Please take a look or bookmark it for your weekend read.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/472?t=8&akid=69%2E4032634%2EsWk6kr) | [](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/472?t=9&akid=69%2E4032634%2EsWk6kr)
---

This is no doubt going to be a fight to get this passed, but I believe this is worth fighting hard for. [**If you agree that Big Tech companies need proper oversight, please pitch in $28 or anything you can so we can continue to fight for this.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/476?t=10&akid=69%2E4032634%2EsWk6kr)
